statement: A string is wound evenly around a cylinder exactly three times, from a point on the bottom rim to the point directly above it on the top rim. The cylinder has circumference 4 cm and height 9 cm. How long is the string?

choices.misconception: I found the length of one turn of the string and stopped there.
I unrolled a single turn but let it climb the full 9 cm height.
I added the distance around three times to the height, as if the string went around and then straight up.
I let each of the three turns climb the full 9 cm height.

hints: Cut the cylinder along a vertical line and unroll it.
Unrolled, the curved surface is a rectangle and each turn of an even winding becomes a straight segment. Placing the three unrolled copies side by side turns the whole string into one straight line.
Three turns side by side make a rectangle 12 cm wide and 9 cm high; the string is its diagonal.

solutions.reliable: Unroll the curved surface into a rectangle 4 cm wide and 9 cm tall. An even winding climbs 3 cm per turn, so each turn is the diagonal of a 4 by 3 rectangle, which is 5 cm, and three turns give 15 cm. The transferable idea: unrolling a cylinder turns a helix into straight segments that the Pythagorean theorem can measure.
solutions.elegant: Lay the three unrolled strips end to end: the string is the diagonal of a 12 by 9 rectangle, which is 15.

whyOnTest: Windings around a cylinder test unrolling a curved surface into a flat rectangle, where a spiral becomes a straight line.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
